transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Millions of people are in the path of a major nor'easter that's strengthening along the
coast.
Heavy rain and strong winds are expected from the Mid-Atlantic into New England.
In New Jersey, the biggest concern is water pushed inland by high winds.
National Weather Service meteorologist Frank Pereira warns that flooding could worsen through
the weekend.
"We're expecting major coastal flooding.
Beginning this morning, Saturday morning with the high tide, repeated rounds of flooding
are unlikely through the weekend.
And with that, we're encouraging people to prepare for significant inundation in low-lying
areas near the shore."
In the Pacific, forecasters are tracking two major storms.
Hurricane Polo is making its way toward Baja California Sur with wind speeds of 165 miles
per hour.
Wind and rain from Hurricane Nolo are starting to come ashore on the Big Island of Hawaii.
Bill Dorman from Hawaii Public Radio reports is the third hurricane to threaten the state
in the last six weeks.
Hurricane Nolo has been lingering off the coast of Hawaii Island for days.
Residents have stocked up on everything from sandbags to drinking water.
The National Hurricane Center says tropical storm conditions will come ashore on the Big
Island with increasing strength overnight, adding that hurricane conditions are possible
on Saturday.
Evacuation centers are open on the island, as well as on Maui, which is also expecting
heavy rain.
Strong and gusty winds are possible for all the Hawaiian islands through the weekend.
For NPR News, I'm Bill Dorman in Honolulu.
President Trump is traveling to Tennessee for a college football game today.
NPR's Danielle Kurtzleben reports it's a matchup of two southeastern conference powerhouses,
the University of Tennessee and the University of Texas.
The president has no other events on his schedule, so it's unclear how much he will be in campaign
mode with midterms just over a month away.
Solidly read, Tennessee has no battleground House, Senate, or Governor's races, though
Texas' Senate race is considered a toss-up.
Trump has worked to make sports a part of his brand this term, holding a UFC match on
the White House lawn, and attending several other sporting events, including the Super
Bowl and the World Cup Final.
The university is offering half-price concessions, including alcohol from 9 to 10 a.m. to incentivize
fans to get in early for the noon game, which will have heightened security for the president's
visit.
Danielle Kurtzleben, NPR News, the White House.
The White House has barred CNN from traveling with the president to Tennessee today.
The network was scheduled to provide television pool coverage of the trip.
Last week, Trump banned CNN, MS Now, and Politico from the White House.
The three outlets have filed a federal lawsuit challenging the decision.
This is NPR News in Washington.
With just over a month until the midterm elections, more campaign ads are using artificial intelligence.
Many states are requiring candidates to disclose its use, but some campaigns are ignoring those
rules.
Experts say, while some altered ads are easy to spot, others are harder to detect.
Alabama has reached a settlement with TikTok, and PR's John Ruich reports the lawsuit accused
the social media company of designing its platform to be "addictive to kids" and "misled
consumers about it."
TikTok has agreed to pay Alabama $100 million, and that figure could go up to $300 million
if certain conditions are met.
A statement from Alabama's attorney general says the short video platform also agreed
to implement a series of safety features designed to protect children.
Those include a two-hour daily time limit extendable by parents, pauses that interrupt
teens using the platform continuously, restrictions on nighttime access, and a prohibition on
cosmetic filters for teen users.
The TikTok agreement follows a similar settlement last month between the social media giant
meta and a group of states, that case also hinged on whether the social media platforms
were designed to hook kids and whether the company was truthful to the public about it.
John Ruich, NPR News.
A jury in New Mexico has found that Facebook misled users about how it protected their
personal information.
The case grew out of the Cambridge Analytica scandal when data from millions of Facebook
users was obtained without their consent.
I'm Windsor Johnston, and you're listening to NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: Major nor'easter strengthens along U.S. coast with heavy rain and flooding expected through weekend
Hurricane Polo approaches Baja California Sur with 165 mile per hour winds
Hurricane Nolo threatens Hawaii's Big Island with tropical storm conditions and possible hurricane conditions Saturday
President Trump travels to Tennessee to attend college football game between Tennessee and Texas
White House bars CNN from providing television pool coverage of Trump's Tennessee trip
Campaign ads using artificial intelligence increase ahead of midterm elections as disclosure rules vary
Alabama reaches $100 million settlement with TikTok over addictive platform design and child safety
New Mexico jury finds Facebook misled users about personal information protection in Cambridge Analytica case
